description: Aggregated posture and trunk geometry screening features derived from per-frame pose estimates for school-based scoliosis risk screening. Features are non-diagnostic and image-based proxies.

trial_id.description: Unique trial identifier within a subject and quest

num_frames.description: Total number of recorded frames in the trial

pose_coverage_ratio.description: Fraction of frames with valid pose detection (pose_present == true)

standing_symmetry_median.description: Median standing symmetry index computed per trial from Q1_standing frames

standing_midline_offset_p95_px.description: 95th percentile horizontal trunk midline offset (in pixels), computed per quest for Q1_standing or Q3_upward_stretch

trunk_curvature_p95_deg.description: 95th percentile 2D trunk curvature proxy derived from upper–lower trunk segment angle difference during Q2_forward_bend

atr_proxy_p95_deg.description: 95th percentile angle-of-trunk-rotation (ATR) proxy derived from 2D trunk curvature during Q2_forward_bend

rib_hump_proxy_p95_px.description: 95th percentile depth-based rib hump proxy (in millimeters or pixels, sensor-dependent) during Q2_forward_bend

trunk_inclination_2d_median_deg.description: Median 2D global trunk inclination angle (image-plane based) aggregated across all quests in the trial

trunk_inclination_2d_p95_deg.description: 95th percentile 2D global trunk inclination angle (image-plane based) aggregated across all quests in the trial

timestamp_start.description: Epoch timestamp of the first recorded frame in the trial

timestamp_end.description: Epoch timestamp of the last recorded frame in the trial

notes.diagnostic_disclaimer: All features are screening proxies derived from 2D pose and depth cues. They do not represent clinical diagnosis, Cobb angle measurement, or medical-grade assessment.
notes.aggregation_note: All scalar features are computed by aggregating per-frame values within a trial using robust statistics (median or 95th percentile).
notes.dimensionality_note: All angular features are image-based (2D). Depth information, where used, serves only as a relative asymmetry cue.
